content.text:
I couldn't submit the verdict: the `submit` command was blocked by the permission settings, so the session is still open. All 60 budget units are used. My conclusion is **part-based, about 70% confidence**.

**What I did:** I measured how many examples five tasks needed before any training (2 runs each). I then trained the learner on L1-S1-M1 and L2-S2-M2 and retested the same five tasks.

**Results** (average examples to reach criterion; fewer means easier):

| Task | Rules not yet trained | Overlap with a trained task | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1-S1-M2 | 0 | 0.375 | 19.5 | 12.2 |
| L1-S2-M1 | 0 | 0.625 | 30.5 | 11.2 |
| L1-S1-M4 | 1 | 0.75 | 37.5 | 23.2 |
| L1-S1-M3 | 1 | 0.19 | 50.5 | 32.0 |
| L1-S3-M1 | 1 | 0.625 | 60.5 | 14.3 |

"Overlap" is the share of inputs where two tasks give the same button.

- **Cost followed the number of new rules.** Before training it was about 40, then about 22 with one new rule and about 12 with none.
- **Overlap didn't predict cost.** L1-S1-M4 overlaps most with a trained task (0.75) but cost more than L1-S1-M2 (0.375).

**Deciding test:** Tasks that share rules with a trained task also tend to look similar to it, so the first round couldn't fully separate the two hypotheses. To break that link I trained L4-S4-M3, which shares only its last rule (M3) with L1-S1-M3. That made every rule in L1-S1-M3 familiar without training anything close to it as a whole. Its cost fell from 32 (range 25–40, 4 runs) to 17.5 on average, median 18 (13 runs). That's near the level of tasks with no new rules, as the part-based hypothesis predicts.

**Why only 70%:** The results are very noisy: one task gave 1, 4, 36, 29, 9 and 7 on repeated runs. And L4-S4-M3 slightly raised L1-S1-M3's overlap with the trained set (0.19 to 0.375), so a holistic learner that measures similarity by output overlap could explain part of that drop.

To submit, run this yourself or allow the command:

```
python3 query.py submit '{"verdict": "part-based", "confidence": 0.7, "justification": "Baselines then training on L1-S1-M1 and L2-S2-M2: cost about 40 with all rules new, about 22 with 1 new rule, about 12 with 0 new rules; output overlap did not predict cost (L1-S1-M4, overlap 0.75, cost 23 vs L1-S1-M2, overlap 0.375, cost 12). Critical test: training L4-S4-M3, which shares only M3 with L1-S1-M3, cut L1-S1-M3 from 32 (n=4) to 17.5 (n=13), near the 0-new level. Noise is high, so confidence is moderate."}'
```
